episode.title: Recover a streamed response after premature transport closure
episode.before: At parent e80d7cc08303c78813508a9ea028f06fd3121e06, the shared retry classifier's exact network-code allowlist did not include ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE. An error carrying that code therefore did not satisfy the network-code retry branch and was not reported under that code by retry telemetry; during streamed response iteration, this prevented the established retry path from recovering solely on the basis of the premature-close code.
episode.after: At f5c0977e96b05f973d664772a6d8962dd12577ba, ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE is an exact member of the transient network-code allowlist. The shared classifier consequently treats the error as retryable and preserves the code as its telemetry error type. A regression test demonstrates a stream yielding incomplete content and then throwing this error, followed by a retry event and a complete response from the next stream attempt.
episode.diff: The implementation adds one network error code to RETRYABLE_NETWORK_CODES in packages/core/src/utils/retry.ts. The accompanying 62-line regression test configures two stream attempts: the first yields an incomplete chunk and throws an Error whose code is ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE; the second yields a STOP-terminated response. It asserts emission of a retry event, delivery of the successful second-attempt chunk, and retry logging with error_type ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE.

evidence_units.claim: Commit f5c0977e96b05f973d664772a6d8962dd12577ba is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 26519, has parent e80d7cc08303c78813508a9ea028f06fd3121e06, and changes the retry utility and streamed-chat network retry test.

evidence_units.claim: The parent retryable network-code list contains connection, DNS, protocol, SSL, and transport-timeout codes but not ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE.

The resolved implementation adds ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE to RETRYABLE_NETWORK_CODES; isRetryableSslErrorCode accepts exact members of this list, isRetryableError returns true when the extracted code satisfies that predicate, and getRetryErrorType returns the accepted code for telemetry.

evidence_units.claim: The streamed-chat regression invokes sendMessageStream and consumes its asynchronous events after the mocked content generator's first stream yields an incomplete chunk and throws ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE; a second generated stream supplies a complete STOP-terminated response.

evidence_units.claim: The regression oracle requires a RETRY event, a CHUNK containing 'Complete response after retry', and a network-retry log record whose error_type is ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE.

candidate_atomics.name: Classify premature stream closure as a recoverable transport failure
candidate_atomics.description: Extend the shared transient-network classification boundary so a prematurely closed response stream enters the existing retry and telemetry path instead of terminating recovery.

semantic_action.intent: Allow an interrupted response stream to be retried and completed by a subsequent attempt while retaining a specific, non-message-based failure classification for telemetry.
semantic_action.module_role: shared transient-network failure classifier used by streamed request recovery
semantic_action.pre_state: A stream attempt can yield partial content and then throw an error carrying ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE, but that code is absent from the exact retryable network-code set.
semantic_action.post_state: An error carrying ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE satisfies the transient network predicate, enters the established retry path, and is categorized under the same code for retry telemetry.
semantic_action.validation: Simulate a first asynchronous stream that yields incomplete content and throws the coded error, then a second stream that completes; assert a retry event, the completed second-attempt chunk, and telemetry containing the exact error code.

candidate_workflows.name: Restore streamed-response progress after a recognized premature closure
candidate_workflows.description: When streamed iteration fails after partial output with a stable transport error code, admit that code into the existing transient-network classifier and verify end-to-end recovery through the stream event and telemetry boundaries.
atomic_names: Classify premature stream closure as a recoverable transport failure

workflow_graph.goal: Convert a premature transport closure during streamed response iteration from a terminal failure into an observable retry followed by successful response completion.
workflow_graph.entry_state: The streaming stack already has retry-event, subsequent-attempt, and retry-telemetry behavior, but its shared classifier does not recognize the premature-close error code.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The premature-close code is recognized as transient; a failed partial stream is followed by a retry event and a successful subsequent stream, with telemetry preserving the code.

steps.action_name: Classify premature stream closure as a recoverable transport failure

unresolved_or_deferred: No separate retry-loop implementation action is extracted because the commit reuses the existing streamed retry machinery and changes only its classification input.
Whether partially emitted content should be reconciled or suppressed across attempts is not asserted by the added test and is therefore deferred.

unresolved_questions: The GitHub bundle does not contain the PR body, reviews, status checks, issue discussion, or author rationale.

No test-run result is present in the supplied bundle, and the repository worktree has its tracked files removed; validation is grounded in the committed regression-test oracle rather than a newly executed test run.

The regression sets getRetryFetchErrors to true, while the implementation's exact network-code check precedes the message-based retryFetchErrors gate; the commit does not explicitly document whether recognition of this code is intentionally independent of that flag.
